main_text.p: plurimùm (si characteres spectamus) αἰ-νιγματώδεας, ac fere hieroglyphicæ, thesaurum tot expetitum votis, hactenus Theo-logis invidissent.

VIII. Sunt hæ quidem omnes, quas sive Veteres, sive recentiores, in authorem Paulum strinxêre objectiones. Nisi jam aliud objectionum genus attendi-mus, quod ipsam Epistolæ canonicam authoritatem & ἀναμάρτητοσίαν vexat. Quarũ aliæ denuò vetustiorum, aliæ recentioris ævi. Illæ binæ potissimùm fuêre, 1. quod faveret Novatianorum impuro dogmati, de lapsis non recipiendis, 11. quod nec ab Arrianorum hæresi videretur aliena, & Christum factum creatumque haud obscurè doceat, de quibus nos libro 1. Cap. VIII. Hæ jam longè plures, motæ à Cajetano, Erasmo, Eniedino, & qui liberiùs de Canonicis variis pronunciarũt. 1. Peccare authorem in sacram Historiam. Dum virgam & urnam in Arca repositas fuisse dicit; dum, Librum fœderis sanguine, simul cum populo, à Mose aspersum; dum, usum hunc in aspersione, lana coccinea, aqua, & hysso
main_text.notes: The running head reads "ad Hebræos:" as printed; the colon is kept. Greek words: "αἰ-νιγματώδεας" and "ἀναμάρτητοσίαν" are copied from the scan but the letters are not fully certain; the ends of the Greek words in the first line are doubtful. The last line of text is cut off at the right edge after "hysso", so the catchword "hysso" is probably "hyssop" with the final letters lost to the edge; it is recorded as the catchword as far as it is visible. Printed numerals "11." and "1." are kept as printed. Long s is written as plain s throughout.
